title: Azure AI Search: enforce Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels at indexing and query time
summary: Pass with corrections: the operational guidance and roadmap facts are supported. The title should distinguish label ingestion during indexing from access enforcement at query time; indexing-time enforcement is not documented. The audit navigation should also acknowledge the different labels in the feature-specific guide.

claims.claim: The feature ingests Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels while indexing documents.
claims.quote: The indexer extracts document content and sensitivity-label metadata.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Query-time enforcement filters documents according to the requesting user's label permissions.
claims.quote: When Purview sensitivity label indexing is enabled, Foundry IQ checks each document's label metadata during query time. It applies access filters based on Purview policies to return only results the requesting user is allowed to access.

claims.claim: When Purview cannot be reached to evaluate policies, standard label-enforced requests fail with 5xx rather than returning partial or unfiltered results.
claims.quote: **Standard label-enforced requests** (with `x-ms-query-source-authorization`): The request fails with `5xx`. Foundry IQ doesn't return partial or unfiltered results when it can't evaluate label policies.

claims.claim: Elevated read bypasses the requesting user's per-document label rights.
claims.quote: Foundry IQ skips the per-document label-based access check and returns matching documents, regardless of the requesting user's `EXTRACT` permissions on each label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Elevated read emits one Purview audit entry for each returned document.
claims.quote: For each document in the response, Foundry IQ emits one entry to the Microsoft Purview audit log on behalf of the requesting tenant. A single search request that returns *N* documents produces *N* audit entries.

claims.claim: Elevated read requires Search Index Data Contributor on the search service or index scope.
claims.quote: The calling developer user must hold the **Search Index Data Contributor** role on the Foundry IQ service or index scope. **Search Index Data Reader** isn't sufficient.

claims.claim: Enabling extraction in an existing pipeline does not reprocess unchanged files in a normal incremental run; backfill requires reset and run.
claims.quote: Enabling extraction, adding metadata fields, or retargeting the pipeline doesn't make unchanged files eligible for a normal incremental run. To reprocess those files, [reset the indexer, then run it](search-howto-run-reset-indexers#how-to-reset-and-run-indexers).
